scenes.visual: pale and dark moths on bark; bark darkens with soot and dark moths become common; air cleans and dark moths become rare; question appears
scenes.tts: Peppered moths rest on trees by day. Some are pale. Some are nearly black. In smoky industrial areas, soot darkened the trees, and dark moths became common. Later the air got cleaner, and dark moths became rare again, in Britain and in parts of the United States. No moth changed its colour. So why do some traits become more common over time?

scenes.visual: a population outline with pale and dark moths; inherited colour from parent to young
scenes.tts: The moths in one wood are a population. A population is a group of the same kind of living thing in one area. Members of a population are not all the same. Some moths are pale and some are dark. Colour is inherited. In this model, young moths have their parents' colour.

scenes.visual: environment chips, bark turns sooty, a bird finds more pale moths than dark ones
scenes.tts: Now add the environment. The environment is everything around a living thing, such as bark, air, food and predators. Here the bark is dark and sooty. Birds spot more of the moths that stand out from the bark. On this bark, the pale moths stand out. So birds find more pale moths than dark ones. Eaten moths have no young.

scenes.visual: survivors reproduce; young have the colour of their parents; one generation
scenes.tts: The moths that are not eaten live to reproduce. To reproduce means to have young. Their young inherit their colour. Most of the survivors here are dark, so most of the young are dark. One step from parents to young is a generation.

scenes.visual: four generations of a sketch population; share of dark moths grows
scenes.tts: Repeat that for many generations. The colour that matched the bark becomes more common. How common a trait is in a population is called trait frequency. In this sketch, the share of dark moths grows each generation. Natural selection shifts trait frequency. It does not change any one moth.

scenes.visual: sooty bark with dark moths, then clean bark; the question answered
scenes.tts: This is natural selection. Individuals with traits that suit their environment are more likely to survive and reproduce. A trait shaped this way, that helps an organism survive and reproduce, is an adaptation. Dark colour on sooty bark was an adaptation. On clean, pale bark, the same colour was not. So why do some traits become more common? Individuals with those traits survive and reproduce more often.
